model_interpretation.claim: The per-pixel turbulence work is likely dominated by repeated gradient evaluation and dependent NoisePerm lookups. Compiler-generated SIMD variants across adjacent x pixels may overlap independent lanes while preserving each pixel's math, but dependent gathers may be costly or scalarized; full-call speedup is uncertain. Let the compiler choose vector width and tail handling, and measure against the valid baseline.

items.subject: SIMD across independent image pixels
items.objective: Test whether mapping adjacent output pixels to SIMD lanes improves end-to-end time on the frozen build and target. Compare explicit SIMD—including the cost of dependent permutation-table gathers—with a simpler compiler-vectorizable formulation where feasible; first preserve the scalar per-lane math to isolate vectorization, then label any further kernel rewrites as separate variants. Do not assume the manual’s vectorization defaults match the actual build flags or that a wider vector is faster. Include tails and full-call costs, validate all specified bounds and sizes at the fixed tolerance, and record failed implementations.
